---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

internalId: f2ec9e28-8064-4707-bce9-b62f24d57524
---

# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor p

While in diagram-view mode, editing a mind map, I have a node selected, then want to use the + sign next to the breadcrumbs -bar, but this is disabled. don't know why. 

I believe it should be possible to add sub diagrams also from mind maps.

## Current state

The breadcrumb **Add child diagram** button observes only the selected item in the saved Current diagram. Editing uses `DiagramSelectionService`, which owns a separate selection for the editable New diagram. Selecting an editable node therefore does not enable the button. This affects every editable diagram type, not only mind maps.

Child diagrams are indexed by a persisted parent diagram ID and item ID. A newly added editable item cannot be a child-diagram parent until the edited copy containing it has been saved and opened.

## Implementation details

* Pass `DiagramSelectionService` to `DiagramBreadcrumbBar` and subscribe to its selection with `useSyncExternalStore` while the active diagram is being edited.
* When the editor selection is non-empty, enable the button only when exactly one selected node or connection has the same ID and kind in the saved Current diagram. Resolve its label from Current so the child context matches its persisted parent. A group, multiple selection, or newly added item remains ineligible.
* When the editor selection is empty, retain the existing Current-selection behavior.
* Open the child action through `DiagramViewService` with the resolved persisted parent. The service must validate that the diagram is active and that the item still exists before creating the child context. Do not copy editor selection into the service's Current selection state.
* Update the breadcrumb and view-service tests. Cover an existing editable mind-map node, another diagram type, Current-selection fallback, multiple selection, group selection, a newly added item, and a stale or missing persisted item.

## Acceptance criteria

* Selecting one existing node in an editable mind map enables **Add child diagram** and opens a child action for that node in the active persisted diagram.
* The same behavior works for one existing node or connection in every supported editable diagram type.
* With no editor selection, a valid Current selection continues to enable the button and open the child action.
* The button is disabled when the editor selection contains multiple objects, a group, or an item that does not exist in Current.
* A newly added editable item cannot receive a child diagram until the edited copy containing it is saved and opened.
* The child action uses the persisted parent diagram ID, item ID, and Current item label.

We should remove this and instead use the default save button on the 'home' tab. When a user edits the diagram, it should, like all other cards and actions and such be saved automatically through the [commit_batcher.ts](app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts)

## Current state

During diagram editing, the Diagram tab shows a separate `DiagramSaveButton`. It calls `DiagramSaveService.save()`, which queues current edited diagram copy and diagram index, then immediately flushes shared commit batch.

Diagram edits already enter normal persistence automatically. `DiagramSaveService` subscribes to model mutations, serializes canonical diagram data, and asks `DiagramViewService` to queue diagram copy and index changes. `DataService.scheduleDiagramCommit()` sends them to `CommitBatcher`, which commits after configured automatic delay. Home-tab Commit button and `Ctrl+S` also flush same pending batch through `ProjectPersistenceService`.

`DiagramSaveService.save()` has two other workflow uses: Review dialog saves before closing, and New diagram creation saves dirty current diagram before switching. Those uses protect workflow transitions and are not duplicate toolbar controls.

## Implementation details

* Remove `DiagramSaveButton` from `DiagramMenuTab`, then remove unused button component and its focused component test.
* Update `DiagramMenuTab` tests to require edit, clipboard, review, metadata, legend, formatting, and comparison controls without a diagram-specific Save/Saved button.
* Keep automatic model-mutation subscription and existing persistence chain: `DiagramSaveService` queues canonical diagram copy plus diagram index through `DiagramViewService`, `DataService`, and `CommitBatcher`. Do not add direct file writes or another diagram persistence path.
* Keep `DiagramSaveService.save()` for Review and New diagram transition workflows. Those operations still require an immediate flush before their next step.
* Keep Home-tab Commit button and `Ctrl+S` as manual immediate-flush entry points. Automatic `CommitBatcher` timer remains normal background persistence path.
* Preserve failure behavior. Queue failures use diagram error dialog; commit failures remain pending, keep edit session dirty, and use project persistence error reporting.
* Retain service tests proving model mutation queues without explicit Save and acknowledgement occurs only after persistence. Add or adjust menu and project-persistence coverage proving diagram changes enable and flush through shared Commit action.

## Acceptance criteria

* Diagram tab contains no diagram-specific Save or Saved control before, during, or after an edit.
* Editing diagram automatically queues canonical diagram copy and diagram index in shared `CommitBatcher`; user does not need to open Home tab or press Save first.
* Queued diagram changes make shared project persistence dirty, enable Home-tab Commit action, and can be flushed with Home Commit or `Ctrl+S`.
* If user takes no manual action, configured automatic commit delay flushes queued diagram and index changes through normal batch flow.
* Successful persistence acknowledges saved copy and clears diagram dirty state only for data included in that commit. Edits made during persistence remain dirty and queue again.
* Commit failure leaves diagram changes pending and editable, with existing user-visible error reporting.
* Review dialog Save and dirty-diagram handling before New diagram creation still complete immediate persistence before closing or switching diagrams.
* Cards, actions, other files, diagram Review behavior, diagram creation, commit batching, push behavior, and read-only behavior remain unchanged.

In the markdown editor, we have a local search function. We should also include a `replace` feature. So the text that was searched for, can be replaced.

* activated through shortcut ctrl+h. this opens the search box expanded so it also contains the `replace` input
* or if the search box is already open, through a dropdown icon, in front of the search text. when expanded, the user can enter the text that needs to replace the selection.
* user can replace selected text or all at once. there should be a button for this

## Current state

`MarkdownEditor` installs `MarkdownLocalTextSearchPlugin` by default. The action-prompt editor opts out because its containing popup owns `Ctrl+F`. Source mode also hides the local visible-text search control. Toolbarless and read-only rich-text editors keep search through `Ctrl+F`.

The plugin opens a non-blocking popup, submits search only on `Enter` or the Search button, and stores submitted term and case mode separately from draft input. It selects next or previous non-overlapping visible-text match, wraps at document boundaries, reports total matches, and supports matches spanning adjacent Lexical text nodes. Search changes selection only; it does not change Markdown, dirty state, history, or persistence.

No replace input, `Ctrl+H` handler, replacement action, or read-only replacement guard exists. Normal Lexical edits already flow through `MarkdownEditor.handleEditorChange` into draft or data-source editing, dirty state, document history, and existing commit behavior.

## Implementation details

* Define **current match** as match selected by last submitted search or later result navigation. Define **Replace all** as replacing every non-overlapping match present when action starts. Replacement text is literal text and is not searched again during same action; an empty replacement is allowed and deletes matches.
* Add an expand/collapse chevron before search field. This is an expansion control, not a menu. Expanded popup adds replacement input plus accessible `Replace` and `Replace all` buttons. Keep existing find controls and non-blocking `Popper` placement.
* Register `Ctrl+H` in editor-local Lexical keyboard handling. Prevent browser history, open popup expanded, preserve selected-text search seeding, and focus search input. `Ctrl+F` and toolbar search button continue opening find-only state.
* Keep draft find term, submitted find term, replacement text, and current match as separate plugin state. Typing either input must not navigate, replace, or change active result count. Search submission remains required before replacement.
* Extend local-search helper with editor operations that replace current matched Lexical range and all current matches, including matches spanning adjacent text nodes. `Replace all` must process initial matches from document end toward start in one editor update so offset changes cannot skip later matches and one undo restores whole action.
* `Replace` changes only current match, then recalculates remaining count and selects next match from end of inserted text, wrapping when needed. Disable replacement actions when no submitted term exists, no current match exists for `Replace`, or editor is read-only. `Replace all` with zero matches leaves document unchanged.
* Pass `readOnly` through local-search plugin configuration. Read-only editors retain find behavior; expanded replacement fields may be viewed, but mutation buttons remain disabled and no edit occurs.
* Let Lexical updates use existing `MarkdownEdi

## acceptance criteria

- Default mode runs the first record in the selected conversation and adds each later record as a new prompt in that same conversation.
- `compact` mode compacts the same conversation after each record before the next prompt starts.
- `new conversation` mode creates one conversation per record and never continues a previous record's conversation.
- Loop mode offers exactly one selected value: `add prompt`, `compact`, or `new conversation`.
- Failure policy defaults to `log and continue`. Each failed record adds a visible failure event to its conversation, and the next record starts.
- `stop on first failure` records the failure and starts no later record.
- Cancelling a loop stops the active work and starts no later record.
- Loop icon appears after the action label and before the prompt-menu button while the displayed conversation has for-each data. Its menu can view persisted JSON, remove it, and change loop settings while idle.

import { SPEED_MODE_OPTIONS, type SpeedMode } from './agent_profiles';

/** Distinguish a requested speed from the tier acknowledged by the provider. */
export function agentSpeedLabel(settings: { speedMode?: SpeedMode; acknowledgedServiceTier?: string | null }) {
    const { speedMode, acknowledgedServiceTier } = settings;
    const requested = speedMode ? `requested speed: ${SPEED_MODE_OPTIONS.find(({ value }) => value === speedMode)?.label}` : '';
    const acknowledged = acknowledgedServiceTier !== undefined ? `provider tier: ${acknowledgedServiceTier ?? 'provider default'}` : '';

    return [requested, acknowledged].filter((value) => !!value).join('; ');
}

Yes. It currently mixes four responsibilities: list layout, sorting, entry formatting, and entry rendering. I’d split it into three focused units—not more.

### Recommended structure

1. `action_run_history.tsx`
   - Owns the “Run history” section layout.
   - Reports `error` through `dialogService`.
   - Reads configured agent accounts once.
   - Renders the ordered entries.

2. `action_run_history_entry.tsx`
   - Owns one history entry.
   - Builds agent/command summaries.
   - Resolves persisted account IDs to current account names.
   - Renders associated `CommitReferenceRow` components.

3. `action_run_history_order.ts`
   - Exports `newestFirstHistoryEntries`.
   - Encapsulates the stable newest-first ordering.
   - Returns the entry plus its source index, as it does today.

This would reduce [action_run_history.tsx](C:\Users\janbo\Documents\dev\md2\app\src\components\actions\run\state\action_run_history.tsx) to roughly 45 lines and give the non-React ordering logic an independent test boundary.

### Suggested ownership

```text
ActionRunHistoryOwner
  └─ loads/subscribes to ActionHistoryStore
      └─ ActionRunHistory
          ├─ reports load errors
          ├─ orders entries
          └─ HistoryEntry
              ├─ formats its summary
              └─ renders commit references
```

I would keep summary construction inside `action_run_history_entry.tsx`. Extracting tiny helpers such as `formatCompletedAt`, `resolveAccountName`, and `agentConfiguration` into separate files would fragment straightforward presentation logic without creating a meaningful reusable unit.

### Test split

- `action_run_history.test.tsx`
  - Empty history.
  - Error reporting.
  - Section rendering.

- `action_run_history_entry.test.tsx`
  - Agent configuration and account-name rendering.
  - Command output rendering.
  - Commit rows and diff interaction.

- `action_run_history_order.node.test.ts`
  - Newest-first order.
  - Tie-breaking.
  - Source array remains unchanged.

### Other cleanup worth including

- Make semicolon usage consistent with the project style.
- Reorder imports consistently.
- Destructure component arguments directly where it improves clarity.
- Preserve the account lookup in the list boundary so every row does not independently subscribe to configuration.
- Preserve the source index for tie-breaking, but recognize it is not durable React identity. The domain type has no run ID, so there is currently no genuinely stable key. I would not invent one during this refactor.
- Keep error reporting in an effect. It correctly avoids throwing or mutating state during rendering.
- Do not move sorting into `ActionHistoryStore`: newest-first order is presentation policy, while the store should retain the loaded model data.

So: yes, splitting is worthwhile, but the clean boundary is three files rather than breaking every formatter into its own helper. No files have been changed.

after: 3cf661d6-03c8-463b-9216-91fb1efc98e0
---

we currently have a lot of components that wrap another component, have the same name as the componet they wrap with '\_owner' appended and just wrap those components in order to pass a prop into them.

This is the wrong architectural approach. we don't want to use this. The idea comes from an instruction that those components need to be self contained: a change in the property should not trigger a render in the parent. Meaning, these should never have been properties. Updates to these properties come from events and this should be handled within the component.

So we need to refactor and remove all those \_owner versions, put the value updates inside the components, remove the properties and replace the '\_owner' versions with the proper components.

ex: `app\src\components\actions\run\popup\action_usage_summary_owner.tsx` and `app\src\components\actions\run\popup\action_usage_summary.tsx`

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

see [action_agent_prompt.tsx](app/src/components/actions/agent/action_agent_prompt.tsx):

* why is it receiving responsePrompts and bottomRow as properties? There must be a very good reason why you wrote the code like this since it is an explicit rule not to do this in the code base.
* when there are 'questions':
  * the component rerenders 8 times, why? can't we improve this
  * the layout is wrong: the questions box always takes up all the available space except for the fixed height of the 'Prompt' box. the way it should work: the prompt box should be minimum size as long as the questions box has not reached the min-content (max-height), the prompt box should fill the remainder of the space and it's content (so the responses bar and markdown editor should use all available space.
* after any edit, for instance in a card, when we switch away from the application while an action popup was open, it will do a full reload 3 times (so with each reload, it will do all the rerenders as described above). This is very strange behavior, nothing changed on the action, yet is still reloads multiple times.
* same thing after closing or opening a card: totally unrelated action popups reload. this is not correct behavior, as nothing about the action popups has changed, no data it relies on has changed.

## Current state

`ActionPromptOwner` owns prompt preparation, draft selection, attachments, scheduling, execution, phrases, and controls, while `ActionAgentPrompt` receives the resulting data and JSX. This separates the feature behavior from the component that should own it and makes `responsePrompts` and `bottomRow` feature-specific JSX properties.

The stores passed through the popup component tree are not global service references. `createActionPopupBindings()` creates `bindingStore`, `conversationStore`, `historyStore`, `inputStore`, `resultStore`, `scheduleStore`, and the layout stores for one selected action and context. `settingsStore` is also a scoped card/action or session/action store returned by a global service. Passing every scoped store separately exposes runtime wiring and creates large forwarding interfaces. The assignment and base contexts are scoped values rather than services; different open popups can have different contexts.

`ActionPopup` subscribes to the complete project state through `useProjectState()`. Any project snapshot replacement therefore rerenders the popup tree, including changes to unrelated cards. Several prompt consumers also subscribe to complete store snapshots while using only one or two fields.

Question display causes a run-state render followed by layout-store updates from 
[1434 characters omitted]
 only the specific scoped store they use. Import true global application services directly when appropriate.
6. Continue passing assignment and base contexts as scoped values. Use `cardInternalId` as card identity; use paths only for loading, persistence, selection references, and continuation inputs.
7. Remove the complete-project subscription from `ActionPopup`. Subscribe separately to the current project reference and the target card fields actually used by the popup: identity, title, worktree assignment, and conversation/activity references. Resolve card subscriptions by `cardInternalId`; paths remain persistence locations and must not become popup identity.
8. Read persisted action state only when selecting the initial action. Do not retain a project-snapshot subscription for that initialization value. Subscribe to historical activity only for historical contexts.
9. Replace complete prompt-store snapshots with stable projections for the values that affect prompt rendering: run status, active action type, interaction readiness, question identity, selected conversation, conversation loading state, and conversion message. Event handlers must read current values directly when a value does not affect rendering.
10. Do not subscribe to schedule card options while the schedule popover is closed. Mount the card-list consumer only while the popover is open.
11. In automatic question layout, size the questions region to its content up to `layout.questionsMaxHeight`. Let the prompt use the remaining height, with the markdown editor flexing while phrase buttons and the bottom row remain fixed. Keep the existing persisted, explicitly resized layout behavior.
12. Publish a layout snapshot only when a layout value changes. A question update may cause one render for the relevant run projection and one additional render only when measurement changes the layout snapshot.

## Acceptance criteria

* `ActionPromptOwner` and its file are removed, and both agent and command flows render `ActionAgentPrompt` directly.
* `ActionAgentPrompt` owns the complete prompt feature and has no `ReactNode`, `responsePrompts`, or `bottomRow` properties.
* `ActionAgentPrompt` receives one `ActionPopupRuntime` instead of separate properties for every runtime store, and no intermediate component forwards those stores individually.
* Two open popups retain separate runtime-store instances and cannot observe or mutate each other's prompt, conversation, history, schedule, result, binding, or layout state.
* Assignment and base contexts remain explicit scoped values and retain `cardInternalId` as canonical card identity.
* Editing, opening, or closing an unrelated card does not render `ActionPopupContent`, `ActionAgentPrompt`, the prompt editor, phrase buttons, or bottom controls in an already open popup.
* Replacing a project snapshot without changing a popup dependency does not reconfigure the popup session or recreate its runtime stores.
* Changing the target card title updates only the target display. Changing its worktree updates only worktree-dependent UI. Changing its conversation/activity references updates only conversation or historical-activity consumers.
* Closed schedule UI does not render because another card changes.
* When questions fit below `questionsMaxHeight`, the questions region uses its content height and the prompt fills the remaining space.
* When questions exceed `questionsMaxHeight`, the questions region is capped and scrolls; the prompt remains at least `promptMinHeight`.
* The markdown editor fills the prompt space not used by phrase buttons and the bottom controls.
* A question update causes no more than one prompt render from run state and one additional render when the measured layout snapshot changes, excluding development `StrictMode` duplication.
* Existing prompt resizing, restored questions, command input, scheduling, phrase insertion, attachments, and keyboard-run behavior continue to work.
* Focused popup and prompt tests pass, including regression tests for unrelated project changes and question layout.

entries.content:
Yes. This file is a strong refactoring candidate, but it should be split by protocol and domain ownership—not merely divided by line count.

[remote_control_storage_service.ts](C:\Users\janbo\Documents\dev\md2\app\src\services\data\remote_control_storage_service.ts) is 1,431 lines and currently owns:

- WebSocket connection lifecycle.
- Request IDs and pending RPC responses.
- Remote error reconstruction.
- Reconnection coordination.
- Eight persistent event/subscription types.
- Event routing.
- `StorageService`.
- `ElectronActionBridge`.
- Codex and Claude runtime bridges.
- Desktop configuration transport.
- Pending-push state.

## Recommended target

| Unit | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `remote_control_client.ts` | Socket lifecycle, request/response correlation, connection events, request IDs, error reconstruction, disconnect and retirement |
| `remote_control_connection_error.ts` | `RemoteControlConnectionError` and its type guard |
| `remote_control_subscription.ts` | Reusable lifecycle for one callback-backed remote subscription |
| `remote_control_broadcast_subscription.ts` | One server subscription shared by multiple local `EventTarget` listeners |
| `remote_control_project_watch.ts` | Project-specific watch registration, errors, restoration, and cleanup |
| `remote_control_action_bridge.ts` | Action commands and action events |
| `remote_control_codex_runtime_bridge.ts` | Codex limits and subscription |
| `remote_control_claude_runtime_bridge.ts` | Claude limits and subscription |
| `remote_control_desktop_config_transport.ts` | Host configuration loading and saving |
| `remote_control_storage_service.ts` | Only `StorageService`, pending-push behavior, lifecycle entry points, and exposure of the composed bridges |

Each class should remain in its own file.

## The first extraction: transport

`RemoteControlClient` should own:

- `WebSocket`.
- `connect`, `disconnect`, and `retire`.
- `ensureConnected`.
- Reconnection waiting.
- Pending request rejection.
- Request serialization.
- Response matching.
- Remote error rehydration.
- Ignoring events from obsolete sockets.
- Best-effort remote unsubscription.
- Connection changes through `EventTarget`.

Domain methods such as `loadProject`, `startAction`, and `getCodexRateLimits` would call the client:

```ts
return this.client.request<StorageProjectFiles>('loadProject', params);
```

This is the safest first step because it separates protocol mechanics while preserving every public method and call site.

## Subscription split

There are three genuinely different subscription models.

1. Callback-backed subscriptions

   Used by action runs, conversation-view changes, rate limits, and merge conflicts. Each local callback gets a corresponding server subscription.

2. Shared broadcast subscriptions

   Used by model catalogs and worktree state. Multiple local listeners share one server subscription. These should use `EventTarget`; listener counts only control the server subscription.

3. Project watches

   Every watched project has separate change, error, and restored behavior. This warrants its own concrete unit rather than adding modes to a generic subscription class.

The existing callback `Set`s are also inconsistent with the current project rule requiring `EventTarget` for listener notification. The extracted subscription units should remove the hand-rolled listener registries.

## Public façade split

After extracting the client, split the five implemented contracts. `RemoteControlStorageService` can expose composed adapters:

```ts
storage.actionBridge
storage.codexRuntimeBridge
storage.claudeRuntimeBridge
storage.desktopConfigTransport
```

The verified consumer changes would primarily be in `remote_connection_service.ts`:

```ts
setActionBridgeOverride(storage.actionBridge);
setCodexRuntimeBridgeOverride(storage.codexRuntimeBridge);
setClaudeRuntimeBridgeOverride(storage.claudeRuntimeBridge);
setDesktopConfigTransportOverride(storage.desktopConfigTransport);
```

The project-opening flow can continue using `RemoteControlStorageService` as `StorageService`. This avoids changing generic storage consumers.

Tests that currently spy on bridge methods directly through `RemoteControlStorageService.prototype` would need to target the appropriate adapter.

## Important behavior to preserve

Several methods look inconsistent but have established behavior:

- `writeFiles` does not mark a pending push.
- Commit, delete, move, integration, and project-config writes do.
- `loadAgentConversation` and `loadActivityConversations` intentionally omit the project argument from the remote request.
- `listRepositories` returns an empty array without contacting the host.
- Requests started during reconnection wait for the shared connection attempt.
- In-flight requests fail on disconnect and are not replayed.
- Subscriptions are restored, but ordinary RPC requests are not.
- Cleanup during asynchronous subscription setup sends an unsubscribe after setup completes.

These should be characterized in tests before moving code.

## Defect discovered

`closeSocket()` clears action-run, rate-limit, merge-conflict, and project-watch subscription state, but it does not clear:

- `conversationViewedCallbacks`
- `conversationViewedSubscriptions`
- `requestConversationViewedEvents`

That creates stale state after a disconnect. More seriously, if the socket closes while a conversation-view subscription is being established, the stale request entry can prevent that callback from being restored.

The current tests verify normal conversation-view delivery but not this reconnect case. This should get a regression test and an explicit decision whether to fix it as part of the refactor. It should not be silently changed as incidental cleanup.

## Test split

The existing test file is roughly 1,600 lines. Split it alongside production code:

- `remote_control_client.node.test.ts`
  - Request correlation.
  - Connection failures.
  - Reconnection waiting.
  - Retirement.
  - Stale socket events.
  - Error reconstruction.

- `remote_control_subscriptions.node.test.ts`
  - Event routing.
  - Restoration.
  - Cleanup during setup.
  - Shared-subscription behavior.

- `remote_control_project_watch.node.test.ts`
  - Changes, errors, restoration, and stopped watches.

- Adapter-specific tests
  - Correct remote method and parameters.
  - Pending-push behavior.
  - Action and runtime bridge behavior.

## Suggested sequence

1. Add missing characterization tests.
2. Decide whether the conversation-view reconnect defect belongs in this work.
3. Extract the connection error.
4. Extract `RemoteControlClient`.
5. Extract subscription lifecycle units.
6. Extract action, runtime, and configuration adapters.
7. Leave `RemoteControlStorageService` as the storage-facing composition root.
8. Split the test file.
9. Perform mechanical cleanup: move the trailing `AgentModelCatalog` import to the import block, initialize fields at declaration where appropriate, normalize semicolons, and reorder imports.

I would not attempt this as one large rewrite. The transport extraction and subscription extraction are independently reviewable boundaries; the adapter split should follow once those tests remain green. No files were changed.

    private closeSocket(socket: WebSocket, error: RemoteControlConnectionError) {
        if (socket !== this.socket) return

        this.connectReject?.(error)
        this.connectReject = null
        this.reconnecting = !this.retired && !this.disconnecting
        this.disconnecting = false
        for (const listener of this.connectionListeners) listener(false)
        for (const pending of this.pending.values()) pending.reject(error)
        this.pending.clear()
        this.actionRunCallbacks.clear()
        this.actionRunSubscriptions.clear()
        this.claudeRateLimitCallbacks.clear()
        this.claudeRateLimitSubscriptions.clear()

entries.content:
Yes—md² is a good topical candidate, but this repository is probably a low-impact promotion channel.

Why it fits:

- The list explicitly accepts AI tools and open-source projects.
- Its **Code & AI Model Tools** section already includes coding-agent orchestrators, desktop agent workspaces, and Git-worktree tools.
- md² supports Codex and Claude Code, so its AI connection is direct rather than incidental.
- Contributions are welcomed through pull requests or issues and only require a link, a 15–20-word description, and tags. [Repository and contribution instructions](https://github.com/dr-mushtaq/Awesome-AI-Tools-Resources)

Why expectations should remain modest:

- The repository currently shows only four stars, despite 40 forks.
- The README is broad and inconsistently curated, with duplicate entries, broken links, formatting errors, and non-AI tools.
- Consequently, inclusion may provide a backlink and some discoverability, but probably little meaningful traffic or credibility.

I would still submit it because the effort is minimal. Place it alphabetically under **💻 Code & AI Model Tools**:

```md
[md²](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2) | Local-first desktop workspace organizing Codex and Claude Code work by Markdown cards, Git worktrees, conversations, and costs. `Coding Agents, Desktop, Open-Source`
```

That description is accurate, fits the requested 15–20 words, and differentiates md² from coding agents themselves: it organizes their work rather than replacing them. See the [md² repository](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2).

# Awesome AI Dev Tools

![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/shvyac/awesome-ai-dev-tools?style=flat)

## Tools

- [WARP CLI](https://developers.cloudflare.com/warp-client/) - Cloudflare WARP client with the `warp-cli` command line: secure, fast connectivity via 1.1.1.1 for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android. *(closed source)*
- [Factory AI](https://factory.com/) - AI coding agents (Droids) for the enterprise; works from desktop, terminal, web, and CLI, and is model agnostic. *(closed source)*
- [CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai/) - AI code review for pull requests: triage, summaries, security checks; works with GitHub and GitLab. *(closed source)*
- [Git Tower](https://www.git-tower.com/) - Powerful Git client for Mac and Windows. *(closed source)*
- [Cursor](https://cursor.com/) - AI coding agent and editor with desktop, CLI, and cloud agents. *(closed source)*

Yes—this is the strongest candidate of the three so far.

Why:

- Its audience is specifically looking for AI developer tools.
- **Agent Orchestrators** explicitly covers tools that run, coordinate, or supervise coding agents—the natural category for md².
- It already lists close peers such as vibe-kanban, automaker, Conductor, crystal, and tools combining Codex/Claude Code with Git worktrees. That strongly validates md²’s eligibility. [See the Agent Orchestrators section](https://github.com/PierrunoYT/awesome-ai-dev-tools#agent-orchestrators).
- It welcomes external submissions and requests concise, neutral descriptions of concrete developer capabilities.
- It is actively maintained: 177 commits, 77 stars, 97 forks, and multiple accepted contributions. [Repository](https://github.com/PierrunoYT/awesome-ai-dev-tools)

The main drawback is saturation: the list contains hundreds of tools, including many worktree-based agent orchestrators. Inclusion will establish md² in the landscape, but the description must emphasize what makes it different—organizing development around persistent Markdown feature cards, rather than merely running parallel terminals.

I would submit md² under the primary **Agent Orchestrators** section:

```md
- [md²](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2) - Local-first desktop workspace that organizes Codex and Claude Code work around Markdown feature cards, Git worktrees, conversations, commits, and usage costs.
```

That is stronger than describing it as another “parallel agent runner.” It captures md²’s distinctive feature-centered model while remaining neutral and concrete, as required by the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/PierrunoYT/awesome-ai-dev-tools/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Priority among the three:

1. **PierrunoYT/awesome-ai-dev-tools** — submit
2. **dr-mushtaq/Awesome-AI-Tools-Resources** — submit if convenient
3. **shvyac/awesome-ai-dev-tools** — revisit after it develops an audience

Your Electron main process is listening on port `9229`.

1. Open Chrome and navigate to:
   `chrome://inspect`

2. Click **Configure…** beside “Discover network targets.”

3. Ensure this target is listed:
   `localhost:9229`

4. Under **Remote Target**, find the Electron/Node process and click **inspect**.

Chrome DevTools opens for the Electron main process. To capture a performance trace:

1. Open the **Performance** tab.
2. Click **Record**.
3. Perform the slow operation in md2.
4. Click **Stop**.

Don’t select the target on port `9222`; that port belongs to the Electron renderer. The project’s profile configuration explicitly starts the main process with `--inspect=9229`. If no target appears, verify that the terminal says `Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229/...`. [Node debugging documentation](https://nodejs.org/learn/getting-started/debugging)

# General feature description

The user should be able to attach a json list (file) to an action so it will run the same action in a loop on the card where each iteration in the loop is for a record in that list (the record becomes a part of the context for the conversation). All editors that can contain placeholders can then also have the 'data' placeholder, which has a second part for selecting the value in the json data.

* On the agent-action-popup, we have a context menu (prompt menu) that currently contains 2 menu items: `compact` & `add file` , we need to add 'for-each' here, which allows the user to select 1 json file that will be attached to the conversation as the 'for-each' data
* the placeholder looks like: `{{data xx.xx.x.xx}}` example `{{data countries.0.cities}}` so countries is a list, we take the item at index 0, field 'cities'
* when an action has a 'for-each' file attached, show a `loop` icon behind the action label in the action button at the top of the action popup. (the loop icon should be something like a horizontal 8)
* also show the loop icon in front of the 'prompt menu' button (vertical dots) that opens the prompt's context menu. The loop icon also opens a context menu where the user can configure the for-each:

# OpenAI Docs

Provide current, cited OpenAI product, API, model, and Codex guidance. Read zero or one primary reference.

**First substantive action:** Search the user's exact requested official OpenAI documentation topic and any explicitly named model using a concise, topic-specific query of 2-6 essential terms. When an already-available direct official documentation search and page-retrieval capability is present, use it first: search, then fetch or open the matching official page before general web search. Otherwise, immediately use official-domain web search, then actually open or fetch the relevant official page. Complete this source order before reading a reference, inspecting local or repository files, running a Codex manual or model resolver, drafting a plan, or answering from memory. Use the actual fetched page, not a search snippet or an unopened link. If one official search or page does not establish the answer, search another appropriate official domain and actually open or fetch the result. Preserve the exact requested model; never substitute a newer model.

**Only exception:** An explicitly requested, genuinely broad, cross-topic Codex setup, orientation, or system-map synthesis may use the manual first when shell execution and an allowed temporary cache are available. A specific Codex feature, setting, command, error, model, or requested citation remains docs-first. Mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons are official documentation questions, not manual-first Codex requests.

For generic software tasks, answer the software task directly. OpenAI implementation, debugging, SDK, API, prompting, agent, and eval requests are not generic.

For a straightforward factual or citation-only request, follow the source order and do not read a route reference. This includes straightforward API facts, ChatGPT Work or mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons, model tiers, aliases, Pro mode, reasoning settings, factual migration baselines, and narrow Codex facts. Prioritize `learn.chatgpt.com` for ChatGPT Work.

## Choose one primary route

Use the first matching route, and read its reference only when the requested task needs that specialized workflow:

- **Explicitly requested local documentation integration:** Read [integration guidance](references/mcp-diagnostics.md) only when the user explicitly requests that local integration.
- **Model migration, upgrades, or model-specific prompting:** Read [model-migration.md](references/model-migration.md) for actual migration planning, implementation, dynamic target resolution, or prompt changes. Preserve an explicitly requested target.
- **Model selection and comparisons:** Read [model-selection.md](references/model-selection.md) only when nuanced current, latest, default, cost, latency, quality, or modality tradeoffs need more guidance. Do not run a migration resolver for selection alone.
- **Product, API, ChatGPT Work, and mixed Chat/Work/Codex documentation:** Read [official-docs.md](references/official-docs.md) only when fetched official pages leave source selection, API schemas, or the requested implementation unresolved. This route is not manual-first.
- **Explicitly broad Codex setup, orientation, or cross-topic synthesis:** Read [codex-self-knowledge.md](references/codex-self-knowledge.md) when the eligible Codex manual or deeper Codex procedures are needed.

Read at most one primary reference. Do not open every route, bundled model guide, or helper script. Read a supporting reference or run a helper only when the chosen workflow demonstrably needs it.

## Source and execution boundaries

- Search, open, fetch, and cite only `developers.openai.com`, `platform.openai.com`, and `learn.chatgpt.com`. Cite the page that supports the claim. State uncertainty when official sources do not establish pricing, availability, account access, limits, or behavior.
- Preserve an explicitly requested model for selection, migration, and prompting. Resolve an unspecified latest or current migration target only after searching and fetching current official guidance.
- Use `references/latest-model.md` only as a disclosed fallback after current official model guidance does not answer the question. Read `references/upgrading-to-gpt-6-astra.md` only for an actual, requested GPT-6 migration; read `references/prompting-guide.md` only for requested prompting work.
- Before building, running, editing, debugging, or testing an API-backed app or tool, use `openai-platform-api-key` first when available. Documentation, conceptual examples, model selection, and read-only guidance do not require an API key.
- Say "OpenAI Docs" or "official OpenAI documentation" in user-facing answers. Keep exact official citations and examples concise.

entries.content: The key distinction is now clear: true structured output constrains the final assistant message, not the agent’s event stream or tool activity. Codex explicitly supports an `outputSchema` on each `turn/start` and documents that it applies only to that turn. Claude also supports a JSON schema, but in the CLI interface md2 uses it is a process-start option; md2’s process lifecycle determines how narrowly it can be scoped.

entries.content:
Yes—JSON can be enforced, and for the for-each use case it should be configured per prompt/turn, not for the complete agent run.

Current situation in md2:

- md2 does not currently expose a response schema.
- Codex’s `--json` and Claude’s `--output-format stream-json` only make the event transport JSONL. They do not constrain the assistant’s answer to JSON. See [agent_profiles.mjs](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/shared/agent_profiles.mjs:29).
- Asking “return only JSON” in the prompt, as diagram actions currently do, is guidance rather than a guarantee.

Provider behavior differs:

- Codex app-server supports `outputSchema` directly on `turn/start`. Official documentation explicitly says it applies only to the current turn, even when later turns continue the same thread. This is exactly the desired granularity. [Codex App Server documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server)
- Claude supports schema-constrained structured output. The installed Claude CLI exposes `--json-schema`, but this is a process-start option rather than a field on each streamed input message. [Claude structured outputs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs)

How that maps to md2:

- Every for-each record calls `executeAgentActionOnce` separately. See [action_run.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:779).
- Each such call starts a new provider process, including when resuming the same conversation. See [agent_runner_service.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:195).
- Therefore, for for-each, a schema can effectively be applied independently to every record for both Codex and Claude.
- For an ordinary long-lived Claude streaming process, the CLI schema would apply to every prompt submitted to that process. Changing it per prompt would require finishing and resuming/restarting the Claude process.
- Codex does not have that limitation: md2 can add `outputSchema` to each individual `turn/start` in [agent_streaming_adapter.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_streaming_adapter.js:269).

Recommended model:

- Add an optional response JSON Schema to an action prompt/run input.
- Apply it to the current turn only.
- For for-each, apply the configured schema separately to every record.
- Do not store it as a global agent setting.
- Parse and validate the final assistant message in md2; currently it remains conversation text even when schema-constrained.
- Treat Codex and Claude implementation differently internally, while exposing one provider-neutral feature.

So the concise answer is: **yes, reliably; per prompt is natively supported by Codex and is effectively achievable per for-each record for Claude because md2 starts a provider process per record.** No files were changed.

entries.content:
A response schema is a JSON Schema document.

In standard JSON Schema, `{}` means “accept any JSON value.” However, provider structured-output implementations use restricted schema subsets, so this is not a reliable cross-provider solution:

- OpenAI requires the root to be an object, requires declared fields, and disallows arbitrary additional properties. [OpenAI Structured Outputs](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs)
- Claude supports all JSON value types, but also requires objects to use `additionalProperties: false`, preventing arbitrary object keys. [Claude structured outputs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs)

Therefore, “any valid JSON” and “schema-constrained JSON” should be separate concepts:

- **JSON mode:** any syntactically valid JSON is accepted.
- **JSON Schema mode:** output must match a specific known structure.

For md2, I would model those as two output modes rather than trying to express “any JSON” through a schema. If portability between Codex and Claude is required, arbitrary JSON would need prompt instructions plus `JSON.parse` validation—and possibly a retry—because the strict schema facilities cannot reliably express arbitrary JSON objects.

Current flow:

- md2 resolves recognized placeholders only in the action prompt before starting the agent ([action_text.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_text.js:29), [action_agent_executor.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_agent_executor.js:78)).
- Thus a prompt such as `Read {{repository-folder}}/{{card-file}}` receives real paths.
- The agent then runs in the repository/worktree and reads that file itself ([agent_runner_service.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:194)).
- Markdown loading returns the raw file contents without placeholder processing ([project_files.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/project/project_files.js:136)).

md2 does briefly load the card to append its `references:` entries to the prompt, but that code only parses the frontmatter; it does not resolve or rewrite its content ([action_card_references.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_card_references.js:61)).

So if the card contains `{{repository-folder}}`, `{{card-file}}`, or another action placeholder, the agent sees that literal text.

Complete this source order before reading a reference, inspecting local or repository files, running a Codex manual or model resolver, drafting a plan, or answering from memory. Use the actual fetched page, not a search snippet or an unopened link. If one official search or page does not establish the answer, search another appropriate official domain and actually open or fetch the result. Preserve the exact requested model; never substitute a newer model.

**Only exception:** An explicitly requested, genuinely broad, cross-topic Codex setup, orientation, or system-map synthesis may use the manual first when shell execution and an allowed temporary cache are available. A specific Codex feature, setting, command, error, model, or requested citation remains docs-first. Mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons are official documentation questions, not manual-first Codex requests.

For generic software tasks, answer the software task directly. OpenAI implementation, debugging, SDK, API, prompting, agent, and eval requests are not generic.

For a straightforward factual or citation-only request, follow the source order and do not read a route reference. This includes straightforward API facts, ChatGPT Work or mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons, model tiers, aliases, Pro mode, reasoning settings, factual migration baselines, and narrow Codex facts. Prioritize `learn.chatgpt.com` for ChatGPT Work.

## Choose one primary route

- **Explicitly requested local documentation integration:** Read [integration guidance](references/mcp-diagnostics.md) only when the user explicitly requests that local integration.

- **Model selection and comparisons:** Read [model-selection.md](references/model-selection.md) only when nuanced current, latest, default, cost, latency, quality, or modality tradeoffs need more guidance. Do not run a migration resolver for selection alone.
- **Product, API, ChatGPT Work, and mixed Chat/Work/Codex documentation:** Read [official-docs.md](references/official-docs.md) only when fetched official pages leave source selection, API schemas, or the requested implementation unresolved. This route is not manual-first.
- **Explicitly broad Codex setup, orientation, or cross-topic synthesis:** Read [codex-self-knowledge.md](references/codex-self-knowledge.md) when the eligible Codex manual or deeper Codex procedures are needed.

Read at most one primary reference. Do not open every route, bundled model guide, or helper script. Read a supporting reference or run a helper only when the chosen workflow demonstrably needs it.

## Source and execution boundaries

entries.content:
It is possible, but a “before reading any file” hook is not a reliable cross-agent solution.

md2 launches the stock Codex or Claude CLI in the worktree ([agent_runner_service.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:194)). It does not currently own the file-reading tool, so there is no md2 interception point between the agent and the filesystem.

Provider behavior differs:

- Claude has `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` hooks for its `Read` tool. `PostToolUse.updatedToolOutput` can replace the content Claude receives, so your proposal can work there. [Claude hooks documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- Codex has `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse`, including for shell calls. However, Codex normally reads through shell commands, and its current hooks cannot directly replace a normal tool result—`updatedMCPToolOutput` is explicitly unsupported. [OpenAI hooks documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks)
- Neither hook system intercepts filesystem access itself. A script, compiler, `rg`, `Get-Content`, or another subprocess can read the file in different ways.

There is also an editing hazard: if an agent reads substituted content but later edits the real file, its expected text does not match what is actually stored. It might fail to apply the edit or write expanded paths back into the card, destroying the placeholders.

The provider-neutral design I would recommend is:

1. md2 loads the current card before starting the agent.
2. It resolves placeholders using the same `resolvePlaceholders` implementation used for prompts.
3. It gives the agent an explicitly labelled rendered snapshot.
4. It keeps the real card path clearly identified as the file to edit.
5. The actual Markdown file remains unchanged.

That snapshot could be either:

- Embedded in the initial prompt—simplest and reliable.
- Written to a per-run rendered file, with instructions to read the rendered file but edit the original—better for very large cards, but adds lifecycle and cleanup concerns.

This works for Codex, Claude, streaming, non-streaming, and custom profiles without depending on provider hooks.

One semantic decision is still needed: I would initially support only the action’s current card. Automatically expanding every Markdown file the agent happens to read is ambiguous—for example, whether `{{card-file}}` in a referenced card means the active card or that referenced card.

Fixed: the placeholder menu now opens at the caret in the card popup, and in the new card dialog too. The affected tests pass (5 files, 37 tests), and lint and typecheck are clean. I haven't checked it in the running app yet; the tests run in jsdom, which has no real layout.

**Cause:** the menu was drawn inside a box that the editor library (Lexical) positions in page coordinates. In the card popup and the new card dialog, that box sits inside a container that is itself positioned on screen. So the menu was pushed right and down by that container's own screen offset.

**Fix:**
- **`markdown_placeholder_typeahead_plugin.tsx`:** the plugin records the caret's on-screen rectangle when the menu opens. It clears it when the menu closes and when the draft is reset. Lexical's box now only decides whether the menu shows.
- **`markdown_placeholder_menu.tsx`:** the menu is placed by an MUI `Popper` anchored to that caret rectangle and attached to `document.body`, so the editor's container no longer matters. It opens below the caret and flips above when there's no room. The z-index that keeps it above the owning popup moved to the `Popper`.

**Tests:**
- New `markdown_placeholder_typeahead_plugin.real.test.tsx`: the editor sits inside an offset container, with the caret rectangle and the viewport size faked (jsdom's viewport height is 0, which otherwise makes the menu flip above). It checks that the menu sits under `document.body` and is positioned at the caret. It would fail on the old code.
- `markdown_placeholder_menu.grouped.test.tsx`: passes the caret rectangle and checks the z-index on the `Popper`.
- `card_body_editor.real.test.tsx` and `new_card_markdown_editor.real.test.tsx`: I removed the check that the menu is inside `overlayContainer`. That check was outdated, since keeping the menu there is what caused the offset. The open, filter and select checks stay.
- `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` passes unchanged.

`status` in `B_271_placeholder_popup_on_card_popup.md` is now `ready`.

import { trackEvent as trackElectronAptabaseEvent } from '@aptabase/electron/renderer'
import { init as initAptabase, trackEvent as trackWebAptabaseEvent } from '@aptabase/web'
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react'
import { getElectronDataBridge } from '../../data/electron_data_bridge'
import { register } from '../service_injector'

export type TelemetryRuntime = 'react_web' | 'react_electron'

export type TelemetryEventName =
    | 'complete_release'
    | 'create_card'
    | 'create_project'
    | 'external_file_import'
    | 'navigation'
    | 'open_project'
    | 'react_start'
    | 'react_stop'
    | 'remarkable_import'

const FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500
const TELEMETRY_EVENTS = new Set<TelemetryEventName>([
    'complete_release',
    'create_card',
    'create_project',
    'external_file_import',
    'navigation',
    'open_project',
    'react_start',
    'react_stop',
    'remarkable_import',
])

function hasValue(value: string | undefined) {
    return typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0
}

function getRuntime(): TelemetryRuntime {
    return getElectronDataBridge() ? 'react_electron' : 'react_web'
}

function settlePendingEvents(events: Promise<void>[]) {
    return Promise.all(events.map(async (event) => {
        try {
            await event
        } catch {
            // Telemetry must not affect application behavior.
        }
    }))
}

/** Owns React telemetry setup and keeps outbound usage payloads detail-free. */
export class TelemetryService {
    private aptabaseEnabled: boolean
    private isStarted: boolean
    private pendingEvents: Set<Promise<void>>
    private runtime: TelemetryRuntime
    private sentryEnabled: boolean
    private trackAptabaseEvent: typeof trackWebAptabaseEvent

    constructor() {
        this.aptabaseEnabled = false
        this.isStarted = false
        this.pendingEvents = new Set()
        this.runtime = 'react_web'
        this.sentryEnabled = false
        this.trackAptabaseEvent = trackWebAptabaseEvent
        this.handleBeforeUnload = this.handleBeforeUnload.bind(this)
        register('telemetryService', this)
    }

    /** Initializes renderer telemetry once during application startup. */
    start() {
        if (this.isStarted) return

        this.isStarted = true
        this.runtime = getRuntime()
        this.trackAptabaseEvent = this.runtime === 'react_electron'
            ? trackElectronAptabaseEvent
            : trackWebAptabaseEvent
        this.aptabaseEnabled = hasValue(import.meta.env.MD2_APTABASE_APP_KEY)
        this.sentryEnabled = import.meta.env.PROD && hasValue(import.meta.env.MD2_SENTRY_DSN)

        if (this.sentryEnabled) {
            try {
                Sentry.init({ dsn: import.meta.env.MD2_SENTRY_DSN })
            } catch {
                this.sentryEnabled = false
            }
        }

        if (this.aptabaseEnabled && this.runtime === 'react_web') {
            try {
                initAptabase(import.meta.env.MD2_APTABASE_APP_KEY)
            } catch {
                this.aptabaseEnabled = false
            }
        }

        this.trackEvent('react_start')
        window.addEventListener('beforeunload', this.handleBeforeUnload)
    }

    trackEvent(eventName: TelemetryEventName) {
        if (!TELEMETRY_EVENTS.has(eventName)) throw new Error(`Unsupported telemetry event: ${eventName}`)
        if (!this.aptabaseEnabled) return

        try {
            const pendingEvent = Promise.resolve(this.trackAptabaseEvent(eventName, { runtime: this.runtime }))
            this.pendingEvents.add(pendingEvent)
            pendingEvent.finally(() => this.pendingEvents.delete(pendingEvent))
        } catch {
            // Telemetry must not affect application behavior.
        }
    }

    captureError(error: unknown) {
        if (!this.sentryEnabled) {
            console.error(error)
            return
        }

            Sentry.captureException(error)

The main cause is missing source maps, not primarily the Sentry library.

- The renderer production build explicitly disables them in [vite.config.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/vite.config.ts:109).
- No `@sentry/vite-plugin`, `sentry-cli`, authentication token, organization, project, or upload command exists anywhere in the build/release pipeline.
- The generated `app/dist` currently contains zero `.map` files.
- Packaging also explicitly rejects all maps in [builder_config.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/packaging/builder_config.js:55).

Consequently, renderer errors point into the approximately 4 MB minified `index-*.js` bundle. Sentry has nothing with which to reconstruct the original TypeScript/React filenames and lines.

The renderer SDK is also incomplete for Electron. It currently initializes only `@sentry/react` in [telemetry_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/telemetry/telemetry_service.ts:3). Sentry’s Electron documentation says Electron renderers should initialize `@sentry/electron/renderer`; for React, its `init` should be combined with the React initializer. This routes renderer events through the Electron main SDK and adds Electron-specific integration. [`@sentry/react` alone can send browser events, but it is not the recommended Electron renderer setup.](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-electron/)

There are two additional capture gaps:

- Renderer Sentry starts only after asynchronous storage initialization in [main.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/main.tsx:26).
- Main-process Sentry starts at [main.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/main.js:210), after many imports and service constructors. Import/startup failures occurring earlier cannot be captured. Sentry recommends initializing both processes as early as possible. [Official Electron setup](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-docs/blob/master/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/electron/index.mdx?plain=1)

Repository history does not show a working source-map uploader. Telemetry was added on July 5, 2026; `sourcemap: false` was made explicit on July 11. Vite already defaults production source maps to disabled, so this appears never to have been reliably configured. What previously looked correct was likely an unbundled main-process stack or a development stack.

The appropriate fix would be:

1. Initialize the renderer through `@sentry/electron/renderer`, combined with `@sentry/react`.
2. Enable hidden production source maps in Vite.
3. Add the official Sentry Vite plugin and upload during the React build using build-only `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, and `SENTRY_PROJECT`.
4. Continue excluding/deleting `.map` files before packaging so customers do not receive them.
5. Move both Sentry initialization points earlier.
6. Add a release verification step that fails if source-map upload fails.

title: aptabase reports usage double
status: ready
owner: 
affects:
agents:

policy:
changedFiles:
