after: 5f556f36-aa43-429a-be26-b901b056e4aa
---

I think we report for both desktop and renderer usage. this is not really needed, preferably, it is the desktop only

## Current state

The desktop app reports to Aptabase from two independent clients that share the same app key. The Electron main process uses `@aptabase/electron/main` in `desktop/src/integrations/telemetry.js` and sends `electron_starting` and `electron_stop`. The React renderer uses `@aptabase/web` in `app/src/services/telemetry/telemetry_service.ts`; `telemetryService.start()` runs from `app/src/main.tsx` in every runtime and sends `react_start`, `react_stop`, and the user-action events with `runtime: 'react_electron'`.

Each client creates its own session ID and its own system properties, so Aptabase counts every desktop launch as two sessions and inflates user and session counts. `@aptabase/electron/main` already registers the privileged `aptabase-ipc` scheme during `initialize`, which `@aptabase/electron/renderer` uses to forward renderer events into the main-process session.

## implementation details

* Add `@aptabase/electron` to `app/package.json` so the renderer can import `trackEvent` from `@aptabase/electron/renderer`.
* In `TelemetryService.start()`, choose the event sender once from the resolved runtime. For `react_electron`, do not call `@aptabase/web` `init` and send events through `@aptabase/electron/renderer` `trackEvent`. For `react_web`, keep the current `@aptabase/web` behavior.
* Keep event names, the `TELEMETRY_EVENTS` validation, the `runtime` property, pending-event tracking, and `flush()` unchanged for both senders.
* In Electron, renderer telemetry follows the main-process Aptabase state: when the desktop has no app key or initialization failed, forwarded events are dropped by the main SDK and must not affect application behavior.
* Leave Sentry setup, `desktop/src/integrations/telemetry.js`, and the desktop events unchanged.
* Update `telemetry_service.service.test.ts`: in the Electron runtime, expect no `@aptabase/web` `init` call and expect events through the mocked renderer `trackEvent`; in the web runtime, keep the existing expectations.

## acceptance criteria

* One desktop launch produces exactly one Aptabase session containing both the `electron_*` events and the renderer events.
* Renderer events sent from the desktop app carry the Electron SDK system properties, such as app version and operating system.
* The web build still initializes `@aptabase/web` and reports its events as before with `runtime: 'react_web'`.
* No Aptabase events are sent from any runtime when `MD2_APTABASE_APP_KEY` is empty.
* Telemetry failures in either runtime never affect application behavior.

title: remove owner components
status: design
owner: 
affects:

policy:
---

we currently have a lot of components that wrap another component, have the same name as the componet they wrap with '\_owner' appended and just wrap those components in order to pass a prop into them.

This is the wrong architectural approach. we don't want to use this. The idea comes from an instruction that those components need to be self contained: a change in the property should not trigger a render in the parent. Meaning, these should never have been properties. Updates to these properties come from events and this should be handled within the component.

So we need to refactor and remove all those \_owner versions, put the value updates inside the components, remove the properties and replace the '\_owner' versions with the proper components.

ex: `app\src\components\actions\run\popup\action_usage_summary_owner.tsx` and `app\src\components\actions\run\popup\action_usage_summary.tsx`

---
author: 
id: J_72
internalId: d9488ddc-6774-41c7-a7cc-eb4aa3283e20
title: restore readable Sentry production stack traces
status: design
owner: 
affects:
agents:
policy:
---

Production renderer errors reach Sentry without the source information required to recover their original TypeScript and React locations. Restore reliable error capture and readable stack traces for the Electron main process and renderer.

## Current state

The React production build explicitly sets `build.sourcemap` to `false` in `app/vite.config.ts`. The build and release pipeline contains no Sentry Vite plugin, Sentry CLI upload, source-map authentication variables, or other source-map upload step. The generated `app/dist` therefore contains minified JavaScript without source maps.

`desktop/packaging/builder_config.js` excludes `*.map` files from both the application package and renderer assets. Excluding maps from the shipped application is correct, but no earlier build step uploads them to Sentry before packaging removes them.

The Electron main process uses `@sentry/electron/main`, but the renderer initializes `@sentry/react` directly. Sentry's Electron SDK expects every renderer to initialize through `@sentry/electron/renderer`. React support is retained by passing the `@sentry/react` initializer to the Electron renderer initializer. The current direct browser client can report renderer errors, but it does not use the Electron renderer integration or route events through the main-process SDK.

Initialization also occurs too late to cover all startup failures:

* `desktop/main.js` loads application modules and constructs services before starting Electron telemetry and registering process error handlers.
* `app/src/main.tsx` starts renderer telemetry only after asynchronous application-storage initialization succeeds.

The main-process source files are shipped as JavaScript without bundling, so their stack locations do not require renderer source maps. Source maps are required for transformed renderer bundles and any future bundled main-process code.

## Implementation details

1. Initialize `@sentry/electron/main` before loading application modules that can fail during import or construction. Register uncaught-exception and unhandled-rejection capture immediately after successful initialization.
2. Initialize the renderer through `@sentry/electron/renderer` and combine it with the `@sentry/react` initializer. Keep React-specific capture behavior while allowing the Electron SDK to coordinate renderer events with the main process.
3. Start renderer telemetry before asynchronous application initialization. Storage startup failures must be capturable without depending on storage initialization succeeding.
4. Add the official Sentry Vite plugin to the renderer build and enable hidden production source maps. The plugin must run after the other Vite plugins so its debug IDs and uploaded artifacts match the final emitted bundles.
5. Upload source maps during `npm run build --prefix app`, before Electron packaging starts. Use build-only `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, and `SENTRY_PROJECT` values. Do not expose the authentication token through an `MD2_` or other Vite client environment prefix.
6. Keep source maps out of the packaged ASAR and installer. Delete them after a successful upload or retain the existing package filters as the final safeguard.
7. Treat a configured production source-map upload failure as a release-build failure. Do not silently produce a release whose renderer errors cannot be symbolicated.
8. Keep `MD2_SENTRY_DSN` as the runtime DSN read by the Electron main process. Renderer initialization must use the Electron SDK's main-process transport rather than creating a separate production client configuration.
9. Set consistent release and environment metadata for main and renderer events if required by the selected Sentry artifact-matching flow. Do not derive domain identity from file paths or release artifact paths.
10. Do not add compatibility branches for the current direct renderer client. Replace it with the Electron renderer integration.

## Build and packaging behavior

The required order is:

1. Build the renderer with hidden source maps.
2. Inject matching Sentry debug IDs into the final renderer bundles.
3. Upload the final JavaScript artifacts and source maps to Sentry.
4. Fail the build if the configured upload fails.
5. Package the application without source-map files.

The Sentry authentication token is a build secret. It must not be written to `desktop/.env`, copied into `resources/.env`, embedded in renderer assets, or included in the installer. The DSN is public runtime configuration and may continue to be packaged through the existing environment flow.

## Tests and verification

* Add focused renderer telemetry tests proving that Electron runtime initialization uses the Electron renderer SDK combined with the React initializer.
* Preserve web-runtime Sentry behavior if the standalone web build remains supported; it may continue to initialize the React SDK directly because no Electron main process exists there.
* Add main-process tests proving that Sentry initialization and process handlers are installed before application services start.
* Add Vite configuration tests for hidden production source maps and the Sentry upload plugin.
* Update package verification tests to confirm that source maps and Sentry upload secrets are absent from the ASAR and installer resources.
* Add a release-build verification that inspects emitted renderer bundles for Sentry debug IDs and confirms that source maps were generated for upload before packaging.
* Perform one production smoke test that captures an error from an application-owned TypeScript/React source file. The Sentry event must show the original file, function, line, and surrounding source context rather than only the minified `index-*.js` location.
* Perform one production main-process smoke test to confirm that an application-owned JavaScript error reports its original file and line.
* Run focused app and desktop tests, both linters, the app type check, and the Windows package verification. Do not run the full test suites unless separately requested.

## Out of scope

* Changing the Sentry project, organization, retention policy, or alert rules.
* Adding performance tracing, session replay, user feedback, or additional personally identifiable information.
* Changing Aptabase telemetry.
* Shipping source maps inside the application package.
* Bundling the Electron main process.

## Acceptance criteria

* Production renderer events use `@sentry/electron/renderer` combined with the React SDK; the main process continues using `@sentry/electron/main`.
* Main and renderer Sentry initialization occurs early enough to capture import, construction, and asynchronous startup failures.
* Every production renderer bundle has a matching source map uploaded to Sentry before packaging.
* A configured source-map upload failure stops the release build with a clear error.
* No source map or Sentry authentication secret is present in the ASAR, unpacked application resources, or installer.
* A production renderer exception displays its original application-owned source file, function, line, and source context in Sentry.
* A production main-process exception displays its original application-owned JavaScript file and line in Sentry.
* Standalone web behavior remains supported if it is currently part of the product, without requiring an Electron main process.
* Existing error reporting and Aptabase behavior remain unchanged apart from earlier Sentry coverage and readable Sentry stack traces.

entries.content:
Yes. You currently use `react-diff-viewer-continued`, rendering complete old/new file contents side by side. There are several better-looking alternatives:

| Option | Best for | Fit here |
|---|---|---|
| **CodeMirror MergeView** | Polished, lightweight editor-style diff | **Best technical fit.** You already use CodeMirror packages, and it accepts old/new text directly. Supports split/unified views and collapsed unchanged sections. Line-click behavior would need a small custom gutter integration. [Documentation](https://codemirror.net/docs/ref/) |
| **react-diff-view** | GitHub-style code review UI | **My visual recommendation.** It supports split/unified layouts, clickable gutters, syntax highlighting, inline changes, decorations and expandable hunks. However, it consumes unified Git diff text, so the desktop diff service would need adjustment. [Project](https://github.com/otakustay/react-diff-view) |
| **Monaco Diff Editor** | VS Code-like experience | Most polished and familiar, with excellent syntax highlighting and navigation. It is considerably heavier, especially because this screen can render several files simultaneously. [React integration](https://github.com/suren-atoyan/monaco-react) |
| **@git-diff-view/react** | Modern GitHub-like appearance | Visually attractive and supports several frameworks, but it is newer and therefore a somewhat riskier dependency. [Project](https://github.com/MrWangJustToDo/git-diff-view) |
| **diff2html** | Traditional GitHub-style patches | Mature, straightforward side-by-side or unified output. Less naturally integrated with React and custom line-click handling. [Project](https://github.com/rtfpessoa/diff2html) |

My preference would be:

1. **CodeMirror MergeView** if we want minimal architectural change and good performance.
2. **react-diff-view** if the main problem is appearance and we want a proper GitHub/code-review experience.
3. **Monaco** only if we explicitly want the VS Code experience and accept the added weight.

A useful additional improvement—independent of the library—would be a split/unified toggle plus collapsing unchanged sections. Those two changes often matter more than the underlying viewer. No files were changed.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity refe

---
author: 
id: J_68
internalId: 83c5615c-4c5c-4c99-8fa6-4ab6e1f61bd5
title: split action run history into focused units
status: ready
owner: 
affects:
agents:
  - design/activity/card__83c5615c-4c5c-4c99-8fa6-4ab6e1f61bd5.json
policy:
after: d2e9440e-e79e-4abe-9092-d786540e29d3
changedFiles:
  - app/src/components/actions/run/state/action_run_history.test.tsx
  - app/src/components/actions/run/state/action_run_history.tsx
  - app/src/components/actions/run/state/action_run_history_entry.test.tsx
  - app/src/components/actions/run/state/action_run_history_entry.tsx
  - app/src/components/actions/run/state/action_run_history_order.node.test.ts
  - app/src/components/actions/run/state/action_run_history_order.ts
---

`app/src/components/actions/run/state/action_run_history.tsx` currently owns the history section layout, entry ordering, agent and command summary formatting, account-name resolution, error reporting, and entry rendering. Split these responsibilities into focused units without changing run-history behavior.

## Current state

`ActionRunHistory` reads the configured agent accounts, reports load errors, sorts entries, formats each entry, and renders the section and commit references. The component is small enough to understand, but its pure ordering behavior and individual entry presentation have no independent boundary. The existing test file consequently covers section behavior, entry formatting, ordering, and commit interaction together.

`ActionRunHistoryOwner` is the only caller. It subscribes to the popup-scoped `ActionHistoryStore`, loads history, and passes `entries` and `error` to `ActionRunHistory`. Agent and command popups each render the owner with their own runtime history store.

`ActionRunHistoryEntry` has no canonical run identifier. The current source index is required to preserve deterministic ordering when completion timestamps match and contributes to the React key, but it must not be promoted to domain identity.

## Implementation details

1. Keep `action_run_history.tsx` responsible for the run-history section, configured-agent-account subscription, error-reporting effect, and rendering of ordered entries.
2. Add `action_run_history_entry.tsx` for one history entry. Move agent and command summary construction, account-name resolution, completion-time formatting, and `CommitReferenceRow` rendering into this component.
3. Pass `accounts` and `entry` to the entry component. Keep the account configuration subscription at the list boundary so each row does not create its own subscription.
4. Add `action_run_history_order.ts` with the pure newest-first ordering operation. Preserve descending `completedAt` order, reverse source order for equal timestamps, and source-array immutability.
5. Keep ordering as presentation logic beside the component. Do not move it into `ActionHistoryStore` or mutate the model entries returned by the store.
6. Preserve the existing error behavior: report each new error through `dialogService` from an effect, reset error deduplication after recovery, and render no history section when there are no entries.
7. Preserve the current compact layout, labels, localized timestamps, agent configuration field order, unavailable-account label, command output, commit rows, and independent diff toggles.
8. Keep the source index for deterministic ties and list keys. Do not add a synthetic or path-based run identity; adding canonical run identity requires a separate domain-model change.
9. Clean up import ordering, component argument destructuring, and semicolon usage in the touched files according to the current project conventions.
10. Do not extract trivial one-line date, label, or account helpers into additional files. Keep entry-specific presentation logic together in `action_run_history_entry.tsx`.

## Tests

* Keep section-level tests in `action_run_history.test.tsx`: empty history, error reporting, and section rendering.
* Add `action_run_history_entry.test.tsx` for agent configuration, current account-name resolution, unavailable accounts, command output, comm
[24287 characters omitted]
by the selected Sentry artifact-matching flow. Do not derive domain identity from file paths or release artifact paths.
10. Do not add compatibility branches for the current direct renderer client. Replace it with the Electron renderer integration.

## Build and packaging behavior

The required order is:

1. Build the renderer with hidden source maps.
2. When `app/.env.sentry-build-plugin` exists: inject matching Sentry debug IDs into the final renderer and worker bundles, upload the JavaScript artifacts and source maps to Sentry, and fail the build if the upload fails.
3. Package the application without source-map files.

The Sentry authentication token is a build secret. It lives only in `app/.env.sentry-build-plugin`. It must not be written to `desktop/.env`, copied into `resources/.env`, embedded in renderer assets, or included in the installer. The DSN is public runtime configuration and may continue to be packaged through the existing environment flow.

## Tests and verification

* Add focused renderer telemetry tests proving that Electron runtime initialization uses the Electron renderer SDK combined with the React initializer.
* Preserve web-runtime Sentry behavior if the standalone web build remains supported; it may continue to initialize the React SDK directly because no Electron main process exists there.
* Add main-process tests proving that Sentry initialization and process handlers are installed before application services start.
* Add Vite configuration tests for hidden production source maps, for no upload plugin without `app/.env.sentry-build-plugin`, and for the upload plugin failing the build when the file is present.
* Update package verification tests to confirm that source maps and the `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` name are absent from the ASAR.
* Perform one production smoke test that captures an error from an application-owned TypeScript/React source file. The Sentry event must show the original file, function, line, and surrounding source context rather than only the minified `index-*.js` location.
* Perform one production main-process smoke test to confirm that an application-owned JavaScript error reports its original file and line.
* Run focused app and desktop tests, both linters, the app type check, and the Windows package verification. Do not run the full test suites unless separately requested.

## Out of scope

* Changing the Sentry project, organization, retention policy, or alert rules.
* Adding performance tracing, session replay, user feedback, or additional personally identifiable information.
* Changing Aptabase telemetry.
* Shipping source maps inside the application package.
* Bundling the Electron main process.

## Acceptance criteria

* Production renderer events use `@sentry/electron/renderer` combined with the React SDK; the main process continues using `@sentry/electron/main`.
* Main and renderer Sentry initialization occurs early enough to capture import, construction, and asynchronous startup failures.
* The app builds and runs from source without any Sentry configuration.
* When `app/.env.sentry-build-plugin` is present, every production renderer and worker bundle has a matching source map uploaded to Sentry before packaging, and an upload failure stops the build with a clear error.
* No source map or Sentry authentication secret is present in the ASAR, unpacked application resources, or installer.
* A production renderer exception displays its original application-owned source file, function, line, and source context in Sentry.
* A production main-process exception displays its original application-owned JavaScript file and line in Sentry.
* Standalone web behavior remains supported if it is currently part of the product, without requiring an Electron main process.
* Existing error reporting and Aptabase behavior remain unchanged apart from earlier Sentry coverage and readable Sentry stack traces.

Replace `react-diff-viewer-continued` with `react-diff-view` for commit and worktree diffs. Preserve opening a changed line in the configured external editor and add session-scoped inline review comments through the new viewer's gutter events and widgets.

## Current state

`DiffView` renders every `DiffFile` with `react-diff-viewer-continued` in split mode. The desktop diff service reconstructs parallel `oldValue` and `newValue` strings from unified Git output and builds arrays that translate viewer-relative line IDs back to repository line numbers. `diff_line_mapping.ts` performs that translation before `openInEditor` is called.

The component has two verified consumers:

* `CommitReferenceRow` expands historical action-run commits.
* `CardCommitDiffPanel` renders a selected non-card file from a historical commit or the assigned worktree. The same panel still uses `DiffFile.oldValue` and `DiffFile.newValue` to render the card body through `MarkdownEditor`.

`react-diff-view` consumes unified patch text rather than two reconstructed strings. It provides split and unified rendering, real old/new line numbers, gutter events, and one widget host per change. The current bridge result does not retain the original patch, and worktree diffs are built from file contents rather than a unified patch.

There is no existing review-comment domain model, persistence format, remote method, or action-message contract. Inline comments in this job are therefore local review annotations owned by the renderer for the current application session. They are not GitHub comments, activity records, agent messages, or durable project data.

## Diff data contract

1. Add `patch: string` to `DiffResult` and `WorktreeDiffResult`. The patch is the canonical input to `react-diff-view`.
2. For commit diffs, preserve the configured diff command and return its unified output as `patch`. Continue validating that the command produced parseable file diffs and continue returning the normalized file metadata needed by existing consumers.
3. Preserve the exact file headers and hunks from the command output. Do not rebuild a commit patch by comparing the reconstructed `oldValue` and `newValue`: those values contain only lines represented by the returned hunks and can lose unchanged gaps between hunks.
4. For worktree diffs, continue reading the base and worktree contents through the existing guarded paths. Add the `diff` package to `desktop/` and generate one unified patch per normalized file from those already loaded values. Use the old path for the old header and the current path for the new header so additions, deletions, and renames remain identifiable.
5. Bound worktree patch generation with the package's abort/complexity option. If a text patch cannot be generated within that bound, fail the diff request with a clear error rather than blocking the Electron main process indefinitely or returning a partial review.
6. Keep `DiffFile.oldValue`, `newValue`, `oldPath`, `path`, and `changeType`; `CardCommitDiffPanel` requires them for the card-body diff and renamed-file navigation.
7. Remove `oldLineNumbers` and `newLineNumbers` from `DiffFile` after all verified cal
[5393 characters omitted]
comment whose target is absent from a newly parsed patch is not rendered. Historical comments remain in the service only while their exact revision is retained; worktree comments are discarded with the replaced revision.
* Repository-root validation before opening an editor remains unchanged.
* Local Electron and remote-control mode must return the same result shape. The remote protocol method names and argument order remain unchanged.
* Existing card-body Markdown diff behavior remains unchanged and continues using the normalized worktree file values.
* Do not add React-version compatibility shims, duplicate viewer modes, or a feature flag for the retired viewer.

## Tests

* Update `desktop/src/git/diff_service.test.mjs` to cover preserved commit patches, multi-hunk files, added/deleted/renamed worktree patches, no-newline markers, generation bounds, and malformed or empty command output.
* Update diff-view tests to cover split rendering, old/new paths, initial-file scrolling, binary fallback, malformed patches, and opening the correct old or new path and real line.
* Add service tests for target identity, stable snapshots, granular events, multiple comments, editing, deletion, draft validation, project clearing, and worktree revision replacement.
* Add user-centric comment-thread tests for opening a composer, saving, cancelling, keyboard handling, editing, deletion, independent old/new targets, and preventing editor opening from comment actions.
* Update bridge and higher-level fixtures that construct `DiffResult`, `WorktreeDiffResult`, or `DiffFile`. Do not add tests that execute Git or another external process; keep the existing runner and filesystem boundaries mocked.
* Run focused app and desktop tests, app type checking, and both linters. Do not run the full test suites unless separately requested.

## Out of scope

* Publishing comments to GitHub, another forge, or a remote review service.
* Persisting comments in card Markdown, activity JSON, project configuration, browser storage, or a new sidecar file.
* Sending comments to an agent, appending them to an action prompt, or adding a submit-review workflow.
* Comment authors, timestamps, replies, resolution state, reactions, permissions, or synchronization between application instances.
* Editing repository content from the diff.
* Expanding omitted context or adding syntax-token workers.
* Replacing the card-body `MarkdownEditor` diff.

## Acceptance criteria

* `react-diff-viewer-continued` is removed and all whole-file commit and worktree diffs render through `react-diff-view`.
* Commit results retain the configured command's exact unified patch; worktree results contain a bounded, valid unified patch generated from their normalized old and new values.
* Split diffs preserve file order, old/new path labels, real line numbers, additions, deletions, modifications, renames, and a safe non-text fallback.
* Clicking an old or new line number opens the correct path and real line in the configured editor.
* Users can add, view, edit, and delete multiple session-scoped comments on commentable old and new lines.
* Comment widgets are accessible, theme-compatible in light and dark mode, and do not trigger line-opening actions.
* Comment state is service-owned, uses `EventTarget` and `useSyncExternalStore`, updates only the affected thread, survives collapse/reopen in the same session, and clears on project or worktree-revision replacement as specified.
* No comment is published, persisted, or sent to an agent, and the UI communicates that comments last only for the current session.
* The card-body Markdown diff, diff error reporting, initial-file navigation, local/remote bridge method names, and repository-root safety checks continue to behave as before.
* Focused tests, app type checking, and both linters pass.

 * clear all comment state when the active project session changes; and
 * replace comments for a worktree revision when a newly loaded worktree result has a different revision.
 
+Give the service a two-phase lifecycle. Its constructor creates no project-dependent state. Initialize it from the application bootstrap with access to the current `DataService` project snapshot and its `changed` event. Compare the canonical project reference fields, clear comment state only when the active project changes, and unsubscribe during application teardown. Do not use the repository root path as project identity.
+
 Do not create comment state during React rendering and do not add a hand-written listener registry, revision counter, or whole-view refresh event. `DiffCommentThread` subscribes at the individual target rendered by its widget so editing one thread does not rerender every file.

 * `diff_service.ts` continues adapting a `CommitReference` to the existing `generateDiff` bridge request and attaching the known repository root to the result.
 * `worktree_service.ts` continues selecting the assigned worktree and calling `generateWorktreeDiff`; it does not own comment state.
 * `remote_control_action_bridge.ts` continues forwarding `generateDiff` and `generateWorktreeDiff` without reshaping their results.
+* `app.tsx` initializes the comment service after the data service exists and provides the project-change subscription used to clear session comments.
